content: The Plasmodiidae family consists of apicomplexan parasites, including the type genus Plasmodium, which is the causative agent of malaria. This family is classified under its own order, the Haemosporida. Diagnostic Criteria The diagnostic features of the Plasmodiidae family include the following: Macrogametes and microgamonts develop independently of each other. Syzygy (the pairing of gametes) is absent. The microgametocyte produces eight flagellated microgametes. The zygote is motile and is referred to as an ookinete. A conoid structure is present only during the ookinete stage. Sporozoites are naked within the oocyst, meaning they are not enclosed within a sporocyst. The life cycle is heteroxenous, meaning that merogony (asexual reproduction) and gamogony (sexual reproduction) occur in the vertebrate host, while fertilization and sporogony (spore formation) take place in the definitive host, which is a blood-sucking insect. Some genera within this family produce hemozoin pigment. Related Genera Currently, several genera are recognized within the Plasmodiidae family. However, as with many protist classifications, these groupings may undergo significant revisions as new DNA sequencing data becomes available. While more comprehensive listings of vertebrate host species can be found on the individual genus pages, typical host species are also noted here.
